hearthstead.guide.attributes.body: Every settler is built from five numbers, 0 to 100: Strength (what they carry, and a blow's force), Stamina (how long a shift they stand), Wits (how fast they learn, and craft precision), Dexterity (fine work at fields, benches, looms) and Spirit (morale under pressure, and how much they lift those near them). A newcomer's five numbers are all capped at fifteen out of a hundred, so nobody arrives a hero — except in their one knack, a single attribute quietly rolled to lean toward that cap instead of away from it.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.body2: Attributes grow only by doing the work that trains them — a lumberer's axe builds Strength, a courier's rounds build Stamina. Growth is slow and never finishes: a settler trained for weeks is one you built. Wits speeds every attribute's growth, itself included, so schooling a clever settler early pays for life. Most settlers carry a trait, sometimes two, and every trait costs something: strong backs carry more and walk slower; quick studies learn faster, a step behind on everything else.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.title: Attributes
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body: Every settler carries a second, quieter number alongside their needs: Dagsverket, the work still in them today. A newcomer starts with twenty units and spends a little every time they finish something — felling a tree, harvesting a crop, closing a production batch, walking a patrol leg — never on a timer, only on work actually completed. Once it runs dry, that trade simply stops taking new work for the day, and whatever a settler already does when idle takes over; nobody needs telling to go rest.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body2: Dagsverket refills at wake, not at midnight, and how much depends on where a settler slept: a real bed gives it back in full, a rough night by the hearth only three-fifths of it — a village of open-air sleepers is visibly less productive than one with real houses. Trained Stamina raises the ceiling itself, so a hardened settler simply gets more day than a green one. A guard's patrols draw on the same pool, though never their sword: answering an alarm or standing a fight costs nothing from it, however tired their legs already are.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.title: Dagsverk
hearthstead.guide.day.body: The whole settlement shares one clock. At Rise everyone wakes and the square fills; through Morning and Afternoon Work they walk to their trade — unless it is farmed or felled, where the work already is. At the midday Meal they gather in the dining hall, and come Evening the tavern and square fill again before Rest sends everyone to bed. A phase is a habit, never a law: a raid or real exhaustion overrides it. Guards keep half their number on a night watch, so someone is always walking.
hearthstead.guide.day.title: The Day
hearthstead.guide.founding.body: Craft a Hearth from logs, cobblestone and a campfire, then set it on open ground, well clear of any settlement already standing. The moment it catches, three settlers gather at the fire and your settlement is born — named, with a working radius around the hearth. Keep bread and other food in its stores: hungry settlers eat there, and a well-fed settlement draws travelers to join it. Break the hearth, and everything tied to it ends.
hearthstead.guide.founding.title: Founding
hearthstead.guide.jobs.body: Jobs are authorised by physical Job Emblems. Learn and register the workplace, then buy its Emblem from the living Mayor. Hold it in your main hand and right-click a compatible settler without sneaking: Hearthstead consumes it once and automatically assigns the nearest valid workplace. There is no separate Hire button. Every new worker starts with no job equipment; their need icon, inventory and Hearth → Requests show the real item they need. Rejected assignments do not consume the Emblem. Empty both hands and Shift-right-click a settler when you want to open their inventory yourself.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.title: Jobs
hearthstead.guide.logistics.body: Workers put finished goods in their workplace chest. The server then publishes a pickup in Hearth → Requests, where every row identifies the item and count, source-to-target route, assigned Courier, current physical owner and Stop reason. A Courier reserves the real stack and moves it from workplace chest to Courier bag to Warehouse; equipment requests move a real tool from Warehouse to the worker's workplace and inventory. Nothing teleports or exists only as a number: containers and bags remain the item authority, and a blocked row tells you why it stopped.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.title: Logistics
hearthstead.guide.mayor.body: One settler speaks for the whole settlement. Appoint a mayor and their knack decides what it grows good at — a strong mayor quickens every trade, a clever one speeds learning, a warm one steadies morale, and so for each of the five. A new mayor's gift takes a day and a half to show, so swapping ahead of a raid you can see coming works, but swapping every morning does not. Losing a mayor is a real blow: morale falls settlement-wide, and the seat sits empty three days before anyone may take it again.
hearthstead.guide.mayor.title: The Mayor
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body: A hung plaque starts blank and does nothing at all — no screen, no scan — until you fit a Build Plan into it. Craft a plan for the building you want and use it on the plaque: that stamps its purpose and sets it surveying the room around it. The plaque glows what it finds: dark while blank, red until something is met, amber once part of the room qualifies, green the moment all of it does.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body2: Every building type wants different things — a house asks for a bed, a door and light; a smithy wants an anvil, a smithing table and a forge nearby. Right-click the plaque to read exactly what your room still needs, ticking off line by line. It re-checks itself every ten seconds on its own, or press Refresh in its own screen to see a change at once.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.title: The Plaque
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.body: A settlement attracts one traveler every two to four Minecraft days, but only while it has a bound Hearth, a valid Tavern, a free bed, morale of at least 60, the full discounted joining price, and enough ready meals to feed everyone for two whole days after that price is simulated. The reserve is eight ready meals per resident after recruitment. An arriving guest waits at the Tavern; if it later invalidates or morale falls, that guest is grandfathered and may still join, but a Hearth, bed, price and post-payment reserve remain mandatory. The base price is four bread and eight planks of any wood. An innkeeper on shift and a standing dining hall each take a quarter off, never deeper than half. Payment leaves the Hearth only at successful admission. Patience is about two and a half days, doubled with an innkeeper, then the traveler moves on.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.title: Recruiting
hearthstead.guide.research.body: The Architect's Study — a lectern flanked by bookshelves — is where a settlement studies itself. Hire a scholar to work there and right-click the lectern to open Prøvebenken, the trial bench: choose one project, pay its cost in paper and a sample of the trade it studies, and the scholar advances it in steady stints at the lectern. An unattended study is not wasted — a small trickle of progress rolls in on its own — but a working scholar is always the real engine. Cancelling a project part-done returns half its sample, never the paper already spent.
hearthstead.guide.research.body2: Six projects are open from the start, each aimed at one part of the settlement's own work: better yeast for the bakery, seasoned timber for the sawmill, iron blestring for the smelter, tanning acid for the tannery, a crop rotation for the fields, and a drill regimen for the guard. Every one finishes into the same shape — a modest, permanent bonus to the work it studies, never a gate — so a settlement that never researches anything still runs, just a little slower than one that does.
hearthstead.guide.research.title: Research
hearthstead.guide.saga.body: Every raid captain who reaches your walls has a name, and one who gets away with what they came for earns a second — 'the Grain-Thief' for one who stole your harvest, 'Larder's Bane' for one who has done it more than once — each a claim you can check against the raid's own report. A captain remembers too: the settler who hurt them most becomes a grudge carried into the next fight, and cutting one down only passes it on — whoever answers next inherits both the grudge and a name sworn to the one who fell.
hearthstead.guide.saga.title: The Saga
hearthstead.guide.summons.body: Right-click a working building's plaque and press Summon to call whoever works there straight to their post — useful for a farmer sleeping off a bad night in the wrong field, or a guard who wandered off to watch instead of fight. A bell rings where you stood; the settler answers with a low murmur wherever they are, then starts walking, glowing the whole way through walls so you can watch them coming. A summons lasts about a minute and a half — past that they simply forget they were called, and the glow fades with it.
hearthstead.guide.summons.title: Summons
hearthstead.guide.threat.body: There is no safe night. Every night rolls its own chance of a raid, between five and fifty-five in a hundred, rather than counting down a fixed timer a player could learn and ignore. A settlement too small or too empty is left alone entirely; grow past that, and the world starts paying attention. Surviving a raid makes you a bigger target, not a safer one — pressure rises when you win, and only eases a little when you lose, because losing costs settlers, buildings and stores.
hearthstead.guide.threat.body2: How dangerous tonight is has a name, and it is never hidden: run /hearthstead info to read your settlement's stage — Rolig (calm), Uro (unease), Varsel (warning) or Beleiring (siege) — beside the raw pressure, tonight's exact chance, and nights since the last attack. One mercy holds at every stage but the worst: a raid never lands the night straight after another, so a settlement just hit always gets one clear night before the world comes calling again.
hearthstead.guide.threat.title: Threat
hearthstead.guide.title: Settler's Handbook
hearthstead.guide.watch.body: A newly assigned Guard starts without a weapon or armour. Their need icon opens a real equipment request: place a serviceable weapon in Warehouse storage and a Courier carries it through their bag to the Barracks and Guard. Open Guard Orders from the settler sheet to choose Hold Here, Defend Hearth, a two-to-eight-point Patrol, or Clear. After Arm the Watch, an Archer assigned to a linked Watchtower can receive the separate Tower Post command. Neither defender can fight properly until the requested physical weapon arrives.
hearthstead.guide.watch.body2: Rank is earned through patrols and real combat, never selected. Each credited hostile kill grants combat XP once and plays the experience cue. Strength unlocks the Guard's later abilities; any rank armour must also exist in settlement storage before it can be worn, so promotion never conjures equipment. The highest-ranked living defender becomes the settlement's captain. Archers follow the same physical-equipment rule for bows and arrows, earn their own combat progress, and return to their persisted patrol or tower order after a fight.
hearthstead.guide.watch.title: The Watch

journey.hearthstead.active_bounded: Complete the current objective to reveal what comes next.

journey.hearthstead.complete.hit: The Hearth survived, but the raid left scars. Review the losses before rebuilding.

journey.hearthstead.step.fj_010_found_he: Place the Hearth and complete founding with all three settlers alive and bound to the new settlement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_020_open_jou: Open the Hearth and choose Journey to see the settlement's next real need.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_030_appoint_: Choose a living settlement member as Mayor. The Mayor authorises research and job emblems.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_100_unlock_l: Open Development at the Hearth and pay the shown physical cost for Timber Rights.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_110_link_lum: Build the plan, then link a valid Lumber Camp plaque and its workplace storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_120_staff_lu: Buy a Lumberer Emblem from the Mayor, hold it in your main hand, then right-click the settler you choose without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_130_open_lum: Empty both hands and Shift-right-click the Lumberer to open their real inventory and requests.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_140_set_lumb: Use the Work Scepter to mark two corners around natural trees, then confirm the exact 3D zone.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_150_lumberer: Let the Lumberer assess the job. Their persistent request shows which physical axes are accepted.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_160_give_lum: Move one compatible physical axe into the Lumberer's inventory or Lumber Camp storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_170_lumberer: Keep a valid natural tree inside the confirmed zone and let the equipped Lumberer complete the work.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_180_lumber_c: The Lumberer must place at least one log from that work action into the Lumber Camp's linked storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_200_unlock_w: Return to Development and pay the shown physical cost for Stores and Roads.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_210_link_war: Build and link a valid Warehouse with registered physical storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_220_staff_wa: Buy a Courier Emblem, hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler with a compatible Warehouse post without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_230_open_req: Open the Hearth, select Requests, press Refresh, and inspect each Courier row: item and count, route, assigned Courier, physical owner and Stop reason.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_240_request_: Leave the real logs in Lumber Camp storage and wait for the Courier system to publish their camp-to-Warehouse pickup row in Hearth → Requests.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_250_courier_: Wait for one Courier to reserve the request and its exact physical stacks.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_260_warehous: The Courier must pick up, carry and deposit the reserved logs into Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_300_unlock_f: Pay the Development cost for Cultivated Ground to learn the Farmhouse plan.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_310_link_far: Build and link a valid Farmhouse with accessible workplace storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_320_staff_fa: Buy a Farmer Emblem, hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler with a compatible Farmhouse post without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_330_set_farm: Use the Work Scepter to confirm a bounded zone containing farmland or planted crops.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_340_farmer_r: Let the Farmer assess the field and publish the exact physical hoe requirement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_350_equip_fa: Move a compatible physical hoe into the Farmer's inventory or Farmhouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_360_supply_f: Place an accepted physical seed in linked Farmhouse storage; the Farmer must withdraw and plant that exact seed inside the confirmed field.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_370_farmhous: The Farmer must harvest a mature crop and place the conserved output in Farmhouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_380_warehous: A Courier must complete the physical crop pickup and deposit it in Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_400_unlock_h: Unlock the Home node to learn the House and Lodging build plans.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_410_link_fir: Build and link a valid House or Lodging so the settlement gains real resident capacity.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_420_unlock_t: Pay the Development cost for Hospitality to learn the Tavern plan.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_430_link_tav: Build and link a valid Tavern before inviting travelers.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_440_recruitm: Meet the live housing, food, safety, morale and Tavern requirements for a recruitment cycle.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_450_traveler: Keep the Tavern valid until the chosen traveler physically arrives and waits for a decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_460_admit_tr: Review the waiting traveler and explicitly admit them as a settlement member.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_500_unlock_f: Pay the Development cost for the First Watch to learn the Barracks plan and Guard Emblem.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_510_link_bar: Build and link a valid Barracks with accessible storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_520_staff_ba: Buy a Guard Emblem, hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler with a compatible Barracks post without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_530_guard_re: Let the Guard assess duty and publish the exact compatible physical weapon requirement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_540_equip_gu: Move one compatible physical weapon into the Guard's inventory or Barracks storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_550_set_guar: Commit a valid Stand Post or Patrol Route assignment for the equipped Guard.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_551_unlock_a: Research Arm the Watch at the Hearth to learn the Watchtower plan and unlock the Archer Emblem and Tower Post command.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_552_add_fift: Keep at least five unique physical bed heads inside valid linked Houses or Lodgings before calling another traveler.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_553_second_r: Keep the Tavern, five beds, food reserve, morale and joining price ready. The next natural attempt, and every retry until this Watch recruit is admitted, qualifies in four to eight minutes.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_554_second_t: Keep the exact linked Tavern valid until this Watch slot's natural traveler physically arrives and waits for your decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_555_admit_fi: Review the waiting traveler, pay the real joining price and explicitly admit them as the settlement's fifth distinct member.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_556_link_wat: Build and link a valid Watchtower with an accessible physical storage container for arrows.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_557_staff_wa: Buy an Archer Emblem, hold it in your main hand and right-click a current settler beside the compatible linked Watchtower without sneaking. The Archer must be a different settler from the Guard.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_558_archer_r: Let the Archer assess the tower and publish the exact serviceable physical bow requirement in the request queue.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559_equip_ar: Supply a serviceable physical bow and let a Courier complete the real request into the Archer's main hand.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559a_supply_: Place at least eight physical Arrows in storage inside this linked Watchtower, then confirm the next Tower Post command; that command verifies the exact rack and advances both facts together.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559b_set_tow: Open Guard Orders for the equipped Archer and choose Tower Post. The commit must point to this linked Watchtower and re-observe its physical arrows.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_560_declare_: With five live settlers, five physical beds, one armed ordered Guard and one bow-and-arrow Tower Post Archer, choose Check Readiness and Declare Ready.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_600_receive_: The persisted raid plan will announce its date, direction and objective before the attack.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_610_first_ra: Defend the settlement until the server records the real raid outcome and losses.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_620_review_a: Open Journey at the Hearth after the raid to review the persisted report and the road ahead.
